cls: EGFR x MET bispecific antibody (antineoplastic monoclonal antibody)
pharm: Bispecific monoclonal antibody targeting EGFR and MET; blocks receptor signaling, drives receptor degradation, and recruits immune effector killing
quick: <80 kg: 1,050 mg IV; >=80 kg: 1,400 mg IV; weekly x4 then q2 weeks
Can cause fetal harm; use effective contraception
Do not breastfeed during and for 3 months after the last dose
No established adjustment; limited data in severe impairment
Infusion reactions, rash/nails/eyes, lung symptoms, VTE signs
summary: Amivantamab (Rybrevant) is an EGFR x MET bispecific antibody for NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations, and in combination with lazertinib (with or without chemotherapy) for EGFR-mutated NSCLC. Dosing is weight-based IV (<80 kg: 1,050 mg; >=80 kg: 1,400 mg) weekly for 4 weeks with the first dose split over two days, then every 2 weeks. Premedicate each infusion and monitor for infusion-related reactions. Key risks are infusion reactions, rash and paronychia, ILD/pneumonitis, ocular toxicity, VTE risk with the lazertinib combination, and embryo-fetal toxicity.
indications: Treatment of adults with locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations after progression on platinum-based chemotherapy
First-line treatment of locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations in combination with chemotherapy
Treatment of EGFR-mutated NSCLC in combination with lazertinib, with or without chemotherapy, per labeling

dosage.c: NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion (single agent or with chemotherapy)
dosage.d: <80 kg: 1,050 mg IV weekly for 4 weeks, then 1,050 mg every 2 weeks. >=80 kg: 1,400 mg IV weekly for 4 weeks, then 1,400 mg every 2 weeks
dosage.n: Confirm EGFR exon 20 insertion before starting; Week 1 dose is split over Day 1 and Day 2 per labeling
dosage.t: Weekly x4, then every 2 weeks until progression or unacceptable toxicity

dosage.c: First-line NSCLC with EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R (with lazertinib, with or without chemotherapy)
dosage.d: <80 kg: 1,050 mg IV weekly for 4 weeks (with lazertinib daily), then 1,050 mg every 2 weeks. >=80 kg: 1,400 mg IV weekly for 4 weeks, then 1,400 mg every 2 weeks
dosage.n: Give with lazertinib per its labeling; VTE risk is higher with this combination and prophylactic anticoagulation is addressed in labeling

dosage.d: Interrupt or slow the infusion for Grade 1-3 reactions; permanently discontinue for Grade 4 or recurrent severe reactions
dosage.n: Premedicate before infusions; have emergency treatment available

admin: Give only as a diluted IV infusion; do not give IV push or bolus
Premedicate before each infusion per labeling (antihistamine, antipyretic, and glucocorticoid for initial doses) to reduce infusion-related reactions
Give the Week 1 dose as a split infusion (Day 1 and Day 2); use the weight-based infusion-rate table and observe during and after infusion
For peripheral versus central line use, follow labeling by week; interrupt, slow, or stop the infusion for reactions and have resuscitation support available
When given with chemotherapy or lazertinib, follow each partner's premedication, antiemetic, and VTE-prophylaxis guidance
moa: Amivantamab is a fully human bispecific antibody that binds the extracellular domains of EGFR and MET. It blocks ligand binding, promotes receptor degradation, and engages immune effector functions (antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity and trogocytosis). This inhibits growth signaling in EGFR-driven NSCLC, including exon 20 insertion disease, and adds MET-pathway blockade.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to amivantamab or any excipient
monitor: Infusion vital signs and symptoms (dyspnea, chills, fever, hypotension) during and after each infusion
Skin, nails, and eyes for rash, paronychia, and ocular toxicity
Signs of VTE, especially with lazertinib combination
relative: History of VTE or VTE risk factors (higher risk with lazertinib combination)

preg: Based on mechanism, amivantamab can cause fetal harm. Verify pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential and advise effective contraception during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on amivantamab in human milk or its effects on the infant or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 3 months after the final dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is established for renal impairment; monoclonal antibodies are not primarily renally cleared. Use with caution in severe impairment and monitor for infusion and organ toxicity.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is established for hepatic impairment; amivantamab has not been adequately studied in moderate to severe hepatic impairment. Monitor for toxicity and for hepatic events when given with hepatotoxic partners.

interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction is described; limit alcohol due to additive constitutional effects.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor infusion vitals; monitor CBC, electrolytes, liver tests, and ocular exams as indicated; evaluate new pulmonary symptoms for ILD.
major: Lazertinib combination - increased VTE risk; follow labeling on anticoagulant prophylaxis and monitor for DVT/PE
Live vaccines - avoid during immunosuppressive cancer therapy
minor: No classic CYP-mediated interactions expected for a monoclonal antibody
moderate: Other agents that cause rash, ILD, or ocular toxicity - additive organ toxicity
Anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents with the lazertinib combination - balance bleeding risk against VTE prophylaxis benefit

common: Infusion-related reactions (dyspnea, chills, fever, nausea, hypotension)
emergency: Severe infusion reaction with breathing difficulty, chest tightness, or hypotension
New or worsening cough, dyspnea, or fever (pneumonitis)
Leg swelling or pain, chest pain, or sudden breathlessness (VTE)
Severe eye pain or vision loss

monitoring: Infusion-related reactions during and after each infusion, especially Week 1
Skin, nails, mouth, and eyes for dermatologic and ocular toxicity
Pulmonary symptoms; withhold and evaluate for ILD/pneumonitis and discontinue if confirmed
Signs of VTE (leg swelling, chest pain, dyspnea), especially with lazertinib
Pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential
counsel: Infusion reactions are most common with the first dose, which is split over two days; premedicines help lower the risk and you will be watched closely
Report rash, painful nails, mouth sores, eye pain or vision changes, new cough or shortness of breath, or leg swelling or chest pain right away
Use sun protection; rash and nail problems are common and early skin care helps
Use effective contraception during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose; do not breastfeed
Tell your team about all medicines; blood-clot risk is higher when this drug is given with lazertinib
pk: Target engagement from first infusion; tumor responses develop over weeks
Dosed weekly for 4 weeks then every 2 weeks to maintain exposure
Refrigerate vials at 2-8 C; protect from light; do not freeze or shake; diluted bags per labeling time limits
pearls: Bispecific EGFR x MET antibody for EGFR exon 20 insertion NSCLC and, with lazertinib, for EGFR-mutated NSCLC; confirm mutation before starting
Weight-based IV dosing (<80 kg: 1,050 mg; >=80 kg: 1,400 mg) weekly x4 then every 2 weeks, with Week 1 split over two days
Infusion-related reactions cluster at first exposure; premedication, split first dose, and rate titration are essential
Dermatologic toxicity (rash, paronychia) and ocular effects need early skin and eye care; ILD requires prompt hold and workup
Lazertinib combination raises VTE risk; follow labeling on prophylactic anticoagulation and VTE monitoring
missed: Amivantamab is given on a supervised infusion schedule, so there is no patient-managed missed dose. If an infusion appointment is missed, contact the oncology team to reschedule as soon as possible; do not attempt to make up doses independently.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for amivantamab overdose. Overdose experience is limited; manage with close monitoring for infusion reactions, skin, pulmonary, and ocular toxicity, and supportive care. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
